answer: For a summit observatory tracking a comet against a sable sky, admission trusts a vendor issuing one certified nonexportable key per chip. A public contract verifies the vendor certificate and the chip's signature over a one-use nonce and account key. It permits one active lease per chip key, grants one vote and escrows 50 tokens for 30 days. Thus n concurrent aliases need n certified chips and 50n locked tokens: linear cost. Anyone can verify certificate chains, nonce consumption, signatures, escrow and expiry on-chain.
